claim.quote: In our final dataset, we report a world-leading energy resolution of 258.5$\pm$0.4 meV in the 1 mm thick detector.

key_value.note: Baseline energy resolution of the 1 mm thick silicon detector.

name: Spontaneous generation of athermal phonon bursts within bulk silicon causing excess noise, low energy background events and quasiparticle poisoning in superconducting sensors
notes: Attached to experiment:spice as well: the TAUP 2025 slides list this resolution under SPICE.

summary.plain: Two nearly identical silicon detectors, one 1 mm thick and one 4 mm thick, showed that spontaneous bursts of vibrations in the crystal itself drive a puzzling excess of low-energy events. The thinner one reached a record energy resolution.
summary.technical: Measurements for 12 days after cooldown of 1 cm^2 silicon athermal-phonon detectors differing only in substrate thickness (1 mm vs 4 mm): channel-correlated shot noise and near-threshold shared LEE relax with time and scale linearly with thickness, pointing to the bulk substrate; the sub-threshold noise energy scale is estimated at 0.68 +- 0.38 meV; final baseline resolution 258.5 +- 0.4 meV (1 mm detector).

title: Spontaneous generation of athermal phonon bursts within bulk silicon causing excess noise, low energy background events and quasiparticle poisoning in superconducting sensors
why_it_matters: The paper argues these bursts are likely a significant source of quasiparticle poisoning in superconducting qubits, and that the low energy excess is a limiting background for low-threshold dark matter detectors.
